subject: Bundling tolerance & SKU swap — request for concession guidance
messages:
From: Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@clinicsuite.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@clinicsuite.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging question — bundling tolerance vs SKU swap

Hi Karthik,

Quick question as we finalize the commercial side: ClinicSuite is trying to consolidate two feature SKUs we currently plan to buy into a single higher-throughput tier to simplify billing. Our procurement team is pushing for a SKU swap (move seats from a modular add-on SKU into the core throughput tier) rather than keeping the two SKUs and applying a bundling discount.

Two constraints on our side:
- We need a firm annual spend ceiling for budget approval.
- We want flexibility to toggle off the add-on later without heavy penalties if usage drops.

Can your team share the typical concession approach here? Specifically: whether Redwood prefers to do a permanent SKU swap (one-time amendment + proration) or keep the SKUs and apply a multi-year bundling credit (with stepdown protections). Also want a sense of how credits vs list-price seat swaps impact renewal math.

If helpful, I attached our updated usage forecast and the proposal you sent last week.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Hale
Director of Platform Ops, ClinicSuite
procurement@clinicsuite.com

Attachments: CLN-7421_proposal_v2.pdf, pricing-workbook.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@clinicsuite.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question — bundling tolerance vs SKU swap

Jordan — thanks for the note and the workbook. Quick answer up front: we can support either path, but they have different operational and renewal implications. Below is a short framing and then I'm looping in Marissa for concession mechanics.

Framing:
- SKU swap (one-time amendment): clean operationally. We amend the SOW, apply prorated charges for the current term, and move the customer onto the new tier. Renewal math treats the swapped seats as part of the core list going forward — good for predictable forecast but reduces visible sprawl of add-ons.
- Bundling credit (credit ladder): keeps the original entitlements intact and applies an annual or multi-year credit against invoice based on agreed thresholds. This preserves the ability to turn an add-on off without contract change but introduces credit reconciliation at renewal and can complicate seat-level metrics.

Tradeoffs for ClinicSuite based on your constraints:
1) If the annual spend ceiling is the primary blocker, a bundling credit capped at the ceiling with a quarterly reconciliation cadence is the lowest-friction from procurement's POV.
2) If you need the option to toggle off quickly without contract amendments, then keep the add-on as-is and use credits.
3) If you prefer a single committed line item for finance (simpler forecasting), the SKU swap + proration is better; we can add a small rollback option (90-day window) for your first renewal to address risk.

I'll include the suggested concession numbers below after Marissa weighs in on discounting bands.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: CLN-7421 - bundling tolerance and concession ask

Marissa / Hannah — Jordan from ClinicSuite asked whether we prefer SKU swap or bundling credit. They want guidance and an example concession. I reviewed and see two viable recommendation tracks; need your input on numbers and approval routing. Quick context:
- Current proposed ARR: $420k list (mix: core tier 80% / add-on throughput 20%)
- Forecasted next-12 usage indicates add-on will grow to 35% of tokens in Q3, then potentially drop if their prod team optimizes prompts (they're cautious).

Recommendations I think we can offer: 
A) SKU swap + proration: Convert add-on seats equal to 25% of current usage into core tier for the remainder of this contract term, apply one-time proration, and provide a 7% permanent list discount on the newly consolidated seats for the first 12 months. Add a 90-day rollback window at renewal with minimal admin fee.
B) Bundling credit (preferred by procurement): Keep both SKUs, apply an upfront annual credit equal to 10% of combined list for year 1, step down to 5% year 2, 2% year 3 (credit ladder). Credit applies only if combined consumption stays above 85% of forecast for each quarter; reconciled quarterly.

Questions for you:
1) Are those concession bands (7% one-time on swap, 10%/5%/2% ladder) acceptable? Any legal/regulatory flags for the rollback option (Hannah)?
2) Which internal approval path should I follow for the SKU swap? I assume pricing desk + revenue ops signoff; does this need SAM exec approval at >$100k concession impact?

I've attached the customer's workbook and our last proposal for reference. If you want to discuss quick, I'm free 3:30–4p PT.

Thanks for the clear framing, Karthik — and appreciate the quick internal loop. Procurement looked at both options and would prefer the bundling credit ladder from a control perspective, but they asked whether the credit could be front-loaded (higher in Q1) to cover our year-one spend ceiling.

We can accept the credit ladder with a slight modification: 12% credit applied in Q1 (to lower initial cash out), then 6% for remaining quarters in year 1, stepping to 4% year 2 and 2% year 3. Credits reconciled quarterly against consumption; any material variance (>15%) triggers a re-eval at renewal.

If Redwood legal is comfortable with that cadence and the credit cap equals the spend ceiling we agreed in the SOW, Procurement is happy to proceed. Once you confirm, we'll route the amendment through our DocuSign flow.

Jordan
Director of Platform Ops, ClinicSuite
